subject: March 3rd service disruption — readout, timeline, and next-step commitments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@cedarbank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cedarbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: March 3rd service disruption — readout, timeline, and next-step commitments

Hi Alex and Priya,

Thanks again for your patience while our team completed the analysis of the March 3rd availability disruption that impacted a subset of your inference requests. Attached is a concise readout (cedarbank-rca-appendix.pdf) plus example logs (tokenization-log-sample.csv) and the remediation workbook (mitigation-plan.xlsx). Please review and call out any immediate questions.

Executive summary (short):
- Incident window: 09:22 — 09:47 UTC, March 3, 2027.
- Impact: elevated tail latency and intermittent 502s for ~8% of requests routed to your dedicated pool; most user-facing requests were retried successfully but a small percentage saw degraded throughput.
- Root cause (brief): a race between autoscaler node-drain and a concurrent cache-eviction routine triggered an inconsistent KV prefix state in ~3 of 18 nodes serving your pool, which caused tokenization and state-lookup failures under load.

Timeline (high level):
- 09:20 UTC — autoscaler initiated a scale-down job after scheduled maintenance window began.
- 09:22 UTC — cache-eviction sweep started to reclaim stale prefixes; eviction scripts ran while node-drain was still rebalancing active sessions.
- 09:24–09:35 UTC — clients routing to affected nodes experienced increased latency and 502s. Automated retry logic mitigated most customer-visible failures.
- 09:47 UTC — failover completed; normal service resumed.

Action items we have completed (short):
1) Hotfix deployed (v3.2.1) to make eviction idempotent relative to node-drain (completed 03/05).
2) Reconfigured the autoscaler to avoid concurrent drains with eviction windows (completed 03/06).
3) Added targeted alerting on prefix-consistency metrics and high-tail tokenization latency (in prod 03/07).

Planned verification steps (what we want to do with you):
- Week of 03/15: run controlled traffic verification with your QA token set and we will supply logs and a runbook for you to validate expected behavior.
- By 03/18: provide a signed verification artifact (shared Drive link in attachments) showing stability under a replay of the incident workload.

Proposed mutual action items (owners and deadlines in mitigation-plan.xlsx):
- Redwood: deliver detailed evidence bundle and runbook (owner: Marissa, due 03/12).
- CedarBank: run verification against your QA set and provide acceptance or outstanding issues (owner: Alex, due 03/18).

Compensation and next steps:
- We are preparing a formal credit calculation per our SLA; initial estimate is a single-month service credit of 10% of March usage tied to the affected routes. We will confirm after the evidence review.

Next steps: please review the attached appendix and let us know whether the verification window week of 03/15 works. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough with our SREs.

Apologies again for the disruption — our priority is to ensure you have a clear, verifiable remediation path and to restore confidence.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0192

Attachments: cedarbank-rca-appendix.pdf (6 pages), tokenization-log-sample.csv (snippets), mitigation-plan.xlsx (actions)
From: Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@cedarbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cedarbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: March 3rd service disruption — readout, timeline, and next-step commitments

Marissa — thanks for the quick readout and the attachments. A couple clarifying questions before we schedule the verification run: 

1) Can you confirm whether any customer PII was at risk or re-processed differently during the degraded requests? We need to evaluate from compliance.
2) For the mitigation you describe (idempotent eviction), can you point to the specific commit or change so our infra team can review the logic?
3) The timeline mentions "most requests retried successfully" — approximately what percentage of our production traffic observed errors that required developer intervention?

Also: Priya in Legal asked whether the proposed credit will be automatic or if we need to open a billing ticket.

If you can answer these in-line we can confirm the 03/15 verification window. We may also request a short call with the SREs during the verification traffic run.

Appreciate the level of detail here.

—Alex
Alex Gordon
VP, Platform Engineering | CedarBank
alex.gordon@cedarbank.com

On Tue, Mar 9, 2027 at 08:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message attached]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@cedarbank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cedarbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T12:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: March 3rd service disruption — readout, timeline, and next-step commitments

Alex — thanks for the questions, answers below inline.

1) PII exposure:
- Short answer: No. The failures were transient tokenization/lookup errors; there is no evidence that any token or customer PII was exported outside Redwood systems. We have included checksums and an S3 evidence bundle in the attachment for CedarBank's compliance review. (See cedarbank-rca-appendix.pdf, section 4).

2) Commit reference for the idempotent eviction fix:
- Commit: 1f9d3b2 (service/eviction: make sweep idempotent vs node-drain). Link: https://redwood.internal/commits/1f9d3b2 (we've also included the patch summary in the appendix).

3) Impact percentage:
- From our ingestion logs, ~8% of routed requests to the dedicated pool experienced an error response (502 or tokenization error). Automated client retries recovered ~85% of those without developer intervention; the remainder required either a client retry outside the built-in window or a user-visible re-try. We list the exact counts in tokenization-log-sample.csv.

Billing/credit process: we will open a billing adjustment ticket on your behalf and the credit will be applied once the verification artifact is accepted. We will share the billing ticket ID in the follow-up.

Proposed mutual action plan (short):
- Marissa / Redwood: provide full evidence bundle + verification runbook by 03/12 (owner: Marissa).
- Alex / CedarBank: execute verification test and report results by 03/18 (owner: Alex).
- Redwood SRE: join verification run for 30 minutes and monitor live (owner: Jonas, calendar invite to follow).

I'll attach the commit diff and the short runbook to the follow-up email. If that timeline looks good, we'll schedule the verification for 03/16 14:00 UTC (tentative).

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: commit-1f9d3b2.diff, verification-runbook.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: March 3rd service disruption — readout, timeline, and next-step commitments

Hannah / Jonas — forwarding the thread with CedarBank; Alex asked about credit mechanics and PII (answered above).

Proposal for exec response and billing:
- Offer a 10% one-month service credit on March billing tied to affected routes (per my note to Alex).
- If we want to be more conciliatory (CedarBank is a strategic mid-market customer), we could offer 15% instead; that would require approval from Finance & Legal.

Requesting:
- Hannah: confirm if you're ok to approve 10% now (fast route) or if you want me to route a 15% approval to Legal/Finance (slower).
- Jonas: please be on standby for the verification run on 03/16 14:00 UTC; I'll send calendar invite once Alex confirms.

I'll hold on the billing ticket until I hear back — Alex requested that we open it proactively but won't finalize credit until verification acceptance.

Thanks,
Marissa

[thread forwarded]
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cedarbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Gordon <alex.gordon@cedarbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: March 3rd service disruption — readout, timeline, and next-step commitments

Marissa / Alex — thanks for the detail and the quick turn. We reviewed the appendix with Legal and Platform. A few notes: 

- We accept the verification window of week of 03/15; 03/16 14:00 UTC works for our QA team. Please send the calendar invite and include the runbook and the commit diff in the event materials.
- We appreciate the proposed 10% credit; CedarBank is willing to accept this as long as the verification artifact is provided and the billing ticket is opened. If Redwood is prepared to offer 15% as a gesture of goodwill, we will pass that to our Finance lead, but 10% is acceptable to move forward.
- Confirmed: no immediate legal escalation on PII based on the evidence summary you shared. We'll complete a deeper compliance review once the full evidence bundle is in our Drive share.

Please proceed with the verification steps and send the invite to the SRE window. We'll expect the evidence bundle by 03/12.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Reliability | CedarBank
priya.shah@cedarbank.com
